books.section: Slavery and the Development of Racism

options.misconception: The entries show change over time, not a fixed and unchanging system.
options.text: Slavery was fixed and unchanging from the first arrival of Africans in Virginia.

options.misconception: No entry abolishes slavery; the 1705 code makes it a lifelong condition.
options.text: Slavery was abolished by Virginia's assembly during the 1600s.

options.misconception: No law in 1619 created slavery; the status was unclear at first.
options.text: Slavery was created by a single law passed in 1619.
Slavery developed gradually, as laws turned an unclear status into a hereditary condition.

rationales.A: The entries show change over time, not a fixed and unchanging system.
rationales.B: No entry abolishes slavery; the 1705 code makes it a lifelong condition.
rationales.C: No law in 1619 created slavery; the status was unclear at first.
rationales.D: The timeline shows a process, not a single moment. In 1619 the status of the first Africans was not yet clearly defined; in 1640 Punch was sentenced to serve for life; in 1662 the partus rule made slavery hereditary; and in 1705 the slave code made it a lifelong condition. Background: Bacon's Rebellion in 1676 sits in the middle, showing planters turning away from servants. No single law created slavery, nothing was abolished, and nothing stayed fixed.
rationales.general:
1. Read the first row. In 1619 the status of the first Africans was not yet clearly defined.
2. Read the last row. By 1705 the slave code defined enslaved people as property for life.
3. Follow the middle rows. A life sentence in 1640, a hereditary rule in 1662, a rebellion in 1676.
4. Name the pattern. An unclear status hardened, step by step, into a hereditary and lifelong condition.
Remember: a timeline is a story — read the first row against the last.

source: original; stimulus is an original data table compiled from the grounding books
stem: Taken together, what do the entries in the timeline best show about slavery in Virginia?

stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from the grounding books; see grounding.
stimulus.text:
| Year | Development |
| 1619 | About twenty Africans arrive in Virginia; their status is not yet clearly defined |
| 1640 | John Punch, an African servant who ran away, is sentenced to serve for life |
| 1662 | Virginia's partus sequitur ventrum law: a child's status follows the mother's, making slavery hereditary |
| 1676 | Bacon's Rebellion: former servants and free Black people unite against the Virginia government |
| 1705 | Virginia's slave code defines enslaved people as property for life |
